chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Husayn ibn Musa, from Ja'far ibn Isa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Mecca and asked me about Abdullah ibn A'ynah. I said, 'He has died.' He said, 'He has died.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then take us to his grave so that we may pray over him.' I said, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'No, but we will pray over him here.' He raised his hands and supplicated, exerting himself in the supplication, and showed mercy to him.

key_terms.تَرَحَّمَ عَلَيْهِ: He showed mercy to him / prayed for his mercy
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Abdullah ibn A'ynah, a known companion

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq do regarding the funeral prayer for Abdullah ibn A'ynah upon arriving in Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility of funeral supplications in Shia jurisprudence, illustrating that the Imam’s emphasis on earnest devotion (*ijtihad*) in prayer outweighs the necessity of physical proximity to the grave. It underscores the scholarly principle that the spiritual merit of the supplication lies in the sincerity and effort of the intercessor rather than the location, a key point in discussions regarding *salat al-janazah* and *du'a* for the deceased.
